evidence_cutoff_scope: Original figures 1-22; later figures carry their own evidence_reviewed_on.
generation: Offline Pillow + standard-library SVG + editable Excalidraw, one shared scene
rendering_limits: Conceptual diagrams are not measured tenant topology, observed plans or performance benchmarks.
PNG uses local Segoe UI. SVG has Segoe UI/Arial fallbacks; Excalidraw uses its Helvetica family.
Excalidraw text has explicit generous dimensions and groups with leaf shapes; font metrics may vary when edited.
Roadmap boundaries are dashed and labeled; preview is not synonymous with coming soon.

figures.title: From operational records to decisions
figures.caption: Conceptual analytics journey: ingest operational data, shape a governed model, and serve decisions while OneLake storage remains separate from compute.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Conceptual responsibility map, not a measured deployment or fixed topology.

figures.title: Fabric's organizing layers
figures.caption: Conceptual containment and assignment map. A capacity supplies compute to an assigned workspace; OneLake is a storage foundation, not a second capacity.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: One illustrative assignment; not a physical infrastructure map.

figures.title: OneLake paths connect readers to data
figures.caption: Conceptual direct and shortcut read paths. An external shortcut references existing data rather than creating an independent authoritative copy.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Reader, shortcut type and source determine supported features and permissions.

figures.title: Three artifacts, three write owners
figures.caption: Conceptual write-ownership lanes for Warehouse, Lakehouse and mirrored database. The mirrored upstream system remains authoritative for source writes.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Mirroring is source-specific. SQL endpoint reads do not transfer ownership of data writes.

figures.title: Choose by the work and its owner
figures.caption: Conceptual decision tree: SQL-managed relational writes favor Warehouse; Spark and file-centered engineering favor Lakehouse. Mixed solutions keep ownership explicit.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: A design aid, not an exhaustive feature matrix or a claim that one path excludes the other.

figures.title: GPU acceleration is a partial execution choice
figures.caption: Conceptual CPU/GPU split: an eligible portion of execution may use GPU acceleration while other work stays on CPU and results are combined.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Illustrative operator split only; not an observed plan, benchmark or universal speedup. Accelerated-workspace metering includes ineligible queries; toggling cancels requests.

figures.title: Authorization depends on the access route
figures.caption: Conceptual security routes. Delegated endpoint mode uses SQL table authorization; user-identity mode uses OneLake roles for underlying table data. Direct storage access is a separate route and does not automatically inherit SQL policy.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: SQL analytics endpoint mode diagram, not a universal Warehouse security matrix. OneLake DDM is not available in user-identity mode; elevated roles require separate review.

figures.title: COPY INTO uses two authorization contexts
figures.caption: Conceptual COPY INTO authorization: the caller retains target INSERT responsibility, while the Fabric-managed workspace identity reads the authorized source.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Workspace Identity COPY INTO is GA as of August 2026. Source-specific role, ACL, network and workspace-membership requirements still apply.

figures.title: QO chooses; DQP coordinates; QE executes
figures.caption: Conceptual query lifecycle distinguishing the query optimizer (QO), Distributed Query Processor (DQP) and local query execution engines (QE).
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Task counts, placement, retries and scheduler algorithms are illustrative, not product guarantees.

figures.title: Commit and publication are different boundaries
figures.caption: Conceptual visibility paths separating Warehouse transaction commit and asynchronous Delta publication from Lakehouse SQL endpoint metadata synchronization.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Not a timing diagram or latency SLA. External readers must verify their required data condition.

figures.title: Metadata sync separates discovery from freshness
figures.caption: Conceptual comparison of legacy background synchronization and new preview metadata sync, where schema discovery and existing-table data freshness are decoupled.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: New sync is preview and opt-in for newly created endpoints; existing endpoints are not automatically upgraded. Query refresh is not synchronous schema discovery.

figures.title: Statistics inform estimates, not business truth
figures.caption: Conceptual diagnostic loop linking distributions, statistics, cardinality estimates, plan decisions and observed execution evidence.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: The return loop is an operator's investigation, not a promised automatic query-feedback feature.

figures.title: Match the evidence to the question
figures.caption: Conceptual evidence map. WarehouseExecutions.OperationId correlates with Query Insights distributed_statement_id, not Capacity Metrics Operation ID.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: WarehouseExecutions and the Data Warehouse Monitor have preview prerequisites. Agentic monitoring is announced, coming soon; available operations diagnostics are bounded, not autofix.

figures.title: Do not confuse three different control points
figures.caption: Conceptual comparison of the existing capacity model and announced on-demand Warehouse model. A compute ceiling queues or slows work; a separate rolling spending limit can pause new operations while in-flight work finishes.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: On-demand Warehouse billing is public preview coming soon at the 9 October 2026 evidence cutoff. Queue discipline, timeouts and rollout details are not published.

figures.title: Cache warmth changes work, not query semantics
figures.caption: Conceptual cache lifecycle: a read may fetch data from OneLake or reuse managed disk and memory caches. Announced cooldown controls are not shown as an existing UI.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Cache cooldown public preview is coming soon. Exact timers, defaults, scope, affected layers and billing are unpublished. Result-set caching is a separate feature.

figures.title: A deployment is a reviewed change, not just a file push
figures.caption: Conceptual release pipeline with schema comparison, a reviewed deployment artifact, one designated pre-deployment script, model deployment, one post-deployment script and validation.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Scripts run every deployment, must be idempotent and are not model-validated at build. Failures halt deployment. Existing Git projects require the documented upgrade.

figures.title: Migrate schema and data as separate workstreams
figures.caption: Conceptual migration plan with parallel schema/logic and data movement workstreams converging on correctness validation and an approved cutover.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Assistant and connector capabilities vary. Watermarks do not propagate deletes; CDC requires a supported CDC-enabled source. No translation equivalence is promised.

figures.title: Business context does not replace the query engine
figures.caption: Conceptual Fabric IQ map. Preview ontology binds business entities to sources; it is not a new storage or query engine. Current IQ MCP supports read-only semantic-model and report discovery plus DAX; Warehouse-specific IQ integration is future.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Optional graph materialization is not a universal execution path. Current IQ MCP does not establish ontology or data-agent support; source execution remains source-specific.

figures.title: Table clone and whole-Warehouse clone differ in scope
figures.caption: Conceptual clone-scope comparison. Current CREATE TABLE AS CLONE OF targets a table; announced whole-Warehouse cloning is a separate forthcoming capability.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Warehouse-level clone public preview is coming soon. No Warehouse syntax, security inheritance or cross-workspace behavior is implied.

figures.title: SQL's logical filter order
figures.caption: Conceptual logical SQL evaluation order: sources and joins, WHERE, grouping and HAVING, window computation, QUALIFY, and final ORDER BY. QUALIFY filters window results.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Simplified reasoning model, not a complete clause grammar or physical plan. New analytical syntax is preview for Fabric Warehouse and SQL analytics endpoints at the evidence cutoff.

figures.title: First Warehouse: create, seed, then reconcile
figures.caption: Concrete high-level walkthrough of the book's Warehouse seed: create BookWarehouse, run 04-create-book-warehouse.sql, then verify the six canonical sales, ten units and 365.00 revenue, with GB 185.00 and DE 180.00.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Expected values are computed offline from the canonical seed, not measured against a live tenant. Run write scripts only in the isolated book lab.

figures.title: First Lakehouse: write with Spark, read through SQL
figures.caption: Concrete high-level walkthrough: create a schema-enabled BookLakehouse, attach it to a Spark notebook, run 05-create-book-lakehouse.py, then verify discovery and read the canonical rows through the SQL analytics endpoint.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: The endpoint is a read surface for Lakehouse tables. Metadata readiness must be verified; no fixed wait guarantees freshness. Expected totals are offline seed checks.

figures.title: Warehouse + Lakehouse: one SQL architecture
figures.caption: Cloud Delta tables and mirrored-database targets are exposed through integration Lakehouse shortcuts beside hosted Delta tables. The Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint serves Warehouse three-part reads, with optional Warehouse-owned gold materialization.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Conceptual current architecture, not a measured deployment or a claim that arbitrary files are SQL tables. Shortcut/source identities, formats and freshness remain separate.

figures.title: Anatomy of a Delta table: values plus valid state
figures.caption: A simplified Delta table combines Parquet data files, JSON transaction actions and checkpoint metadata. Warehouse SQL commit, background Delta publication and an authorized external reader observing that state are separate boundaries.
figures.conceptual_status_caveat: Conceptual format/publishing map, not a private Warehouse directory layout. A checkpoint holds metadata, not another batch of business rows; external access does not automatically inherit SQL RLS or CLS.
